title: ‘Water isn’t enough’: As extreme heat devastates farms, community wisdom is more vital than ever
content: My intention was to write about simple self-sufficiency, especially when it comes to growing food. But then this summer was challenging in a way I thought I was prepared for... but wasn't.

title: Big solar vs. forests: Why we remain determined to save these trees
content: The veneration of solar has taken up the oxygen in the climate conversation. While we have a modest array ourselves, I'm worried solar has been presented to the climate-worried public as a panacea, as if a wholesale switch to solar would stabilize the climate.

title: What do we still share in an age of political polarization?
content: Deepening fragmentation reflects an urgent challenge: our growing difficulty in identifying what truly matters, and therefore in designing policies that promote our collective well-being.

title: Sammy Gensaw: The restorative revolution and a river of reciprocity
content: In this keynote address, Indigenous activist Sammy Gensaw shares his experiences working for ecological and cultural revival along the Klamath River, central to his people’s identity and livelihood.

title: US Forest Service to clearcut one of the last great groves in the Tongass. Here’s how to save it
content: It’s referred to as Unit 346 in the Twin Mountain II timber sale. On the ground, it’s some of the most spectacular old-growth we’ve ever witnessed, and it’s marked for clearcutting.

title: How ice and rock triggered Nepal’s catastrophic flood – and why climate change is raising the risks
content: The catastrophic flood that killed hundreds of people in Nepal in August shows the ways rising temperatures, thawing permafrost and melting ice are increasing the risk of destructive floods in the Himalayas and other regions around the world.

title: A future of ‘fewer and less’ may be unavoidable. But how do we get there humanely?
content: With age, I’ve become more aware of the world’s complexity but also better equipped to come to simple, albeit painful, conclusions: We need to replace fantasies of endless growth with ideas about managing the contraction.

title: ‘Earth keeps a ledger, and it is written in water’: Reflections on hurricanes, water cycles and inheritance
content: My family has feared water, depended on it, and moved uphill from it for four generations. The watching was never the point. What we did with what we saw was the point.
